findings.message: The pre-push verdict rule and the CI verdict-coverage rule disagree on how many commits may follow the reviewed sha: pre-push admits only head or head's FIRST PARENT, CI admits any ancestor whose whole delta is verdict evidence.
findings.detail_md:
Two independently authored predicates now govern the same artifact:

| Gate | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| pre-push, `specs_canon.verdict_violations` | a `verdicts/<40hex>.handoff.json` file is conformant only if its sha equals `head_sha` or `parent_sha` (head's first parent) | `dadaia_workspace/features/specs/specs_canon.py:148-173` |
| CI, `pr-verdict-check.sh` | a verdict covers the PR head if its `metrics.commit_sha` is the head OR any ancestor of it, AND every differing path is itself verdict evidence | `.github/scripts/pr-verdict-check.sh:293-324` |

Reproduced directly against the shipped predicate:

```
verdict_violations([... , 'releases/0.5.0/verdicts/<reviewed>.handoff.json'],
                   head_sha=<commit C that ADDS the verdict>,
                   parent_sha=<reviewed>)              -> []          # push allowed
verdict_violations(same paths,
                   head_sha=<any commit D on top of C>,
                   parent_sha=<C>)                     -> [that path] # push BLOCKED
```

So the verdict commit must be the LAST commit before the push. One further commit of any kind -- a typo fix, an empty commit, a second verdict file -- turns the just-approved verdict into a canon violation and refuses the push until the file is deleted. Adding a fresh verdict for the new head does not help on its own: the new file and the deletion of the old one must land in ONE commit.

**Direction of failure: CLOSED, and no bypass exists.** The asymmetry cannot be used to pass an unreviewed head: landing non-evidence code after the verdict makes `pr-verdict-check.sh` SKIP that handoff (a non-evidence path appears in `git diff --name-only <sha> <head>`), and `--no-verify` bypasses only the pre-push side, never the CI job. It is an availability and usability trap, not a security hole.

Related note, benign: on a merge commit `first_parent` is the previous target-branch tip, so a feature-branch verdict would read stale -- but `develop` and `main` are never pushed directly, so the pre-push canon gate never evaluates a merge commit.
findings.fix_recommendation: Do not widen `verdict_violations` by adding a second allowed-sha branch. Make the two gates share ONE predicate: express the CI rule's real invariant -- 'the verdict names a commit whose delta to head is verdict evidence only' -- and have the pre-push side call it, or state explicitly in `specs/releases/AGENTS.md` that the verdict commit is required to be the final commit before the push and that re-verdicting replaces the old file in the same commit. Whichever is chosen, one rule, one home.

findings.message: atomic_write(expected_previous=...) narrows the compare-then-swap window but does not close it -- the comparison and os.replace remain two separate syscalls, so a writer landing between them is still silently discarded.
findings.detail_md:
CWE-367 (time-of-check time-of-use race).

`dadaia_workspace/core/atomic_write.py:103-113`:

```
if expected_previous is not None:
    ...
    current = path.read_bytes() if binary else path.read_text(encoding='utf-8')
    if current != expected_previous:
        raise ConcurrentModificationError(path)
os.replace(tmp, path)
```

The module docstring's claim -- 'nothing but the comparison itself sits between the read and the swap' -- is literally true and the window is far narrower than the caller-side read-before / re-read-after pattern it replaces (which is the real bug it closes). But narrow is not atomic: a `read()` followed by an unconditional `rename()` is not a compare-and-swap. A concurrent writer that lands in that window is still lost with every command exiting 0 -- the exact symptom of the bug this parameter was introduced to fix, at a much lower probability. Consumers are the three JSONL record stores' rewrite paths (`infrastructure/jsonl_record_store.py:117,152`).

**Impact is bounded and low:** the affected files are local governance ledgers on a single-operator machine, not an authentication or authorization store, and the workspace's own no-locks doctrine deliberately accepts surfaced races. Recorded because the docstring reads as a closure claim, and a future reader may build on it as if it were one.

Two related observations on the same seam, neither a defect:
* the temp sibling is created with the process umask, not the target's mode, unless `preserve_mode=True` and the target already exists -- fine for these world-readable ledgers, worth remembering before this primitive is ever pointed at a restricted-mode file;
* `path.read_text(encoding='utf-8')` raises `UnicodeDecodeError` on a corrupt live file, which propagates and refuses the write with the temp file cleaned up -- fail-closed, correct.
findings.fix_recommendation: Leave as is for the local-ledger use case, but replace the docstring's closure phrasing with what it actually guarantees ('narrows the window to a single comparison; not an atomic compare-and-swap'). If a genuinely atomic seam is ever needed, do it by holding an `O_EXCL` lock sibling for the compare-and-rename pair rather than by adding another parameter to this function.

findings.message: Two of the three new JSONL record models ship with no redaction seam: FindingRecord and AdrRecord have no .redact(), and by their own docstrings both are written to committed files by agents with plain file tools, bypassing the write-time masking BugRecord and BacklogHistoRecord get.
findings.detail_md:
This is the same defect class as the closed bug `backlog-histo-writer-skips-write-time-denylist-redaction`, one fold later.

| Model | Write-time redaction | Write seam |
|---|---|---|
| `core/models/bugs.py::BugRecord` | `.redact(denylist_terms)` at `:317`, applied by `features/bugs/service.py:181` and `:195` | CLI |
| `core/models/backlog.py::BacklogHistoRecord` | `.redact(denylist_terms)` at `:330` | CLI |
| `core/models/findings.py::FindingRecord` | **none** | none -- its own docstring: '`specs/audits/**` has no CLI writer ... project-auditor and the remediation closure both append/rewrite FINDINGS.jsonl with file tools' |
| `core/models/adr.py::AdrRecord` | **none** | none -- its own docstring: '`specs/ADRs/**` has no CLI writer ... an agent proposes/accepts/supersedes an ADR with plain file tools' |

So a finding or an ADR carrying an operator-local absolute path, an address literal, an internal hostname or an operator denylist term is written verbatim into a committed, ADDITIVE (ungated) file. `core/redaction.py::redact_text` is now a shared, domain-agnostic primitive that either model could call, and the diff moved it there precisely so a second model would not have to copy it -- these two do neither.

**Backstop, verified in this review:** the pre-push denylist scan refuses the push on the packaged baseline (`infrastructure/data/privacy_baseline.json`: ipv4-literal, ipv6-literal, internal-hostname, home-abs-path, users-abs-path, windows-users-path, email-address, secret-token) plus the operator denylist. The baseline file is unchanged by this diff. The failure mode is therefore a refused push, not a leak -- which is why this is LOW and record-only. The residual gap is only the class of sensitive content the baseline does not model.
findings.fix_recommendation: Give `FindingRecord` and `AdrRecord` the same `.redact(denylist_terms)` method their two siblings already have, routed through `core/redaction.py::redact_text` -- no new primitive, no per-model regex copy. Because neither has a CLI writer today, the method has no caller until one exists; the higher-value alternative is to state in `specs/audits/AGENTS.md` and `specs/ADRs/AGENTS.md` that the authoring agent redacts before writing, and let the push scan stay the enforced boundary. Operator picks; either way the asymmetry should be deliberate rather than incidental.

findings.message: The .gitignore inversion drops the catch-all privacy backstop for specs/memory/** without carrying the local-notes.md / tmp/ scratch denies that every other newly opened area received.
findings.detail_md:
CWE-538 (insertion of sensitive information into an externally accessible file).

The diff replaces the old `specs/*` catch-all plus per-artifact whitelist -- correctly, since that shape caused nine registered bug recurrences -- with per-area opt-in, everything TRACKED BY DEFAULT. Finding F-20 of the prior cycle carried the scratch denies to the newly opened areas:

```
/specs/audits/**/local-notes.md        /specs/audits/**/tmp/
/specs/ADRs/**/local-notes.md          /specs/ADRs/**/tmp/
/specs/bugs/_archive/**/local-notes.md /specs/bugs/_archive/**/tmp/
/specs/backlog/_archive/**/...         /specs/releases/**/...
```

`specs/memory/**` is opted in wholesale (`!/specs/memory/`, `!/specs/memory/**`) and received no such pair, so `specs/memory/local-notes.md` or `specs/memory/tmp/scratch` would be staged by default.

**Compensating control, verified in this review:** the NEW pre-push specs-canon gate refuses any path under `specs/` that is not canon-conformant, and neither `memory/local-notes.md` nor `memory/tmp/...` matches any pattern in `features/specs/specs_canon.py::_CANON_FILE_PATTERNS` (memory admits only `AGENTS.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `QUALITY.md`, `TECHSTACK.md`, `product/index.md`, `product/catalog.json`, `product/<area>/<slug>.md`). The push is blocked, not leaked. This is genuinely the stronger control -- the gitignore backstop hid the file silently, the canon gate names it -- which is why the inversion improves the posture overall.
findings.fix_recommendation: Either add the two scratch denies for `specs/memory/**` for symmetry with the other five areas, or -- better, and in this release's own direction -- record explicitly in the .gitignore comment block that `specs/memory/**` relies on the specs-canon gate alone, so the omission reads as a decision rather than a miss.

findings.message: JsonlRecordStore.append writes a record through a buffered text handle, so a serialized line larger than the stream buffer is split across multiple write syscalls and O_APPEND no longer covers the whole record.
findings.detail_md:
`dadaia_workspace/infrastructure/jsonl_record_store.py:79-84`:

```
line = json.dumps(self._to_dict(record), sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False) + '\n'
with self._path.open('a', encoding='utf-8') as handle:
    handle.write(line)
```

The docstring states 'O_APPEND semantics -- race-benign'. That holds only while the record fits the default 8 KiB buffer: past it, CPython issues several `write(2)` calls, and two concurrent appends can interleave mid-record, producing two corrupt lines. Not theoretical for this ledger -- several records in the migrated `BUGS.jsonl` carry `symptom` + `repro` + `root_cause` + `evidence_*` free text well past 8 KiB (visible in the migration diff).

Blast radius is contained by the reader: `iter_records` skips a malformed line with a logged WARN, and `update`/`remove` copy an unparseable line through verbatim, so a torn record is dropped from views but never silently rewritten. An availability and record-integrity issue on a local ledger, not an access-control one.
findings.fix_recommendation: Make the single append a single syscall: open the file in binary append mode and issue one `os.write` of the encoded line, or wrap the handle so the line is flushed as one buffer. One call site, no new branch. Then the docstring's 'race-benign' claim becomes true for every record size.

findings.message: JsonlRecordStore's warning logs interpolate the ledger's absolute path, and the model-parse arm interpolates a ValueError that can carry record field content -- no redaction is applied on the logging path.
findings.detail_md:
CWE-532 (insertion of sensitive information into log file), defence-in-depth.

`dadaia_workspace/infrastructure/jsonl_record_store.py:187`, `:190` and `:195` all log `self._path` -- an absolute filesystem path that necessarily contains the operator's home directory segment, the exact shape `core/redaction.py::_POSIX_HOME_RE` exists to mask everywhere else in this codebase. `:195` additionally interpolates the exception raised by `self._from_dict(raw)`; a `ValueError` from the model layer can quote the offending field value.

These go to the stdlib logger, not to a committed record or a handoff, so nothing crosses the publication boundary on its own -- but a captured CI log or a pasted terminal transcript carries them, and this repository has a registered history of exactly that class.
findings.fix_recommendation: Log the ledger by a repo-relative name rather than the absolute path, and drop the exception object from the model-parse arm (the record id or the line ordinal is enough to locate the bad line without echoing its content).

findings.message: The specs-CLI complexity ratchet contract test now skips itself in CI: pytest.importorskip('radon') was added under a comment stating CI does not install radon, so the ratchet it enforces never runs where it is meant to gate.
findings.detail_md:
`tests/contract/test_specs_cli_complexity_ratchet.py:34` (added at 412ef54a):

```
pytest.importorskip('radon')  # CI does not install radon; ruff C901 is the CI-side ceiling
from radon.complexity import cc_visit  # noqa: E402
```

A contract test that is unconditionally skipped in the environment it exists to gate is a silent-skip: it turns green without asserting anything, and no signal distinguishes 'ratchet held' from 'ratchet not measured'. DADAIA.md section 7 treats skipping as a stewardship decision requiring evidence, and the same commit's pyproject comment documents that radon and ruff genuinely disagree on this codebase (radon reports 61 where ruff C901 reports 63 for `features/panel/handler.py::make_handler_class`, bug `radon-undercounts-nested-class-in-function-complexity-vs-ruff-c901`), so the two are not interchangeable measurements.

**Compensating control:** `ruff check .` DOES run in CI with `max-complexity = 63`, so a complexity regression past the enforced ceiling still fails the build. The lost coverage is the radon-specific ratchet, not the ceiling itself. Not a security control -- recorded as a test-integrity observation and routed to qa-engineer.

**A second, DIFFERENT skip landed at 95bc2e56 and is NOT the same class.** `tests/contract/test_pr_verdict_check_gate.py:33-36` replaces its `pytestmark` with `skipif(sys.platform == 'win32')`, reason 'POSIX bash CI script; the Windows runner's bash is the WSL stub'. That one is correctly scoped: the `security-verdict-gate` job it guards is `runs-on: ubuntu-latest` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:505`), so the platform where the script actually executes still runs the full suite -- verified, 383 targeted tests including this file pass here. The `contract` marker is not lost either: `tests/conftest.py`'s `_PATH_MARKERS` auto-marks everything under `tests/contract/` by path. No finding against it; recorded so the two skips are not conflated.
findings.fix_recommendation: qa-engineer decides: either install radon in the CI job that runs the contract tier so the ratchet actually executes, or delete this test and let ruff C901 be the single ceiling. A permanently skipped contract test is the one outcome to avoid.

findings.message: Residual of the resolved MEDIUM 1: releases_histo.jsonl classifies MUTATING while the other three areas' _archive histo files classify ADDITIVE, so the law's single ADDITIVE row is honoured by three of four areas.
findings.detail_md:
Measured against the shipped classifier at fa021900, not inferred:

| Path | Class |
|---|---|
| `specs/bugs/_archive/bugs_histo.jsonl` | ADDITIVE |
| `specs/backlog/_archive/backlog_histo.jsonl` | ADDITIVE |
| `specs/backlog/_archive/consumed_backlog_histo.jsonl` | ADDITIVE |
| `specs/audits/_archive/audits_histo.jsonl` | ADDITIVE |
| **`specs/releases/_archive/releases_histo.jsonl`** | **MUTATING** |

`DADAIA.md:67` states the ADDITIVE row as 'each area's `_archive/*_histo.jsonl`'. `releases_histo.jsonl` is such a file -- it is admitted by the canon (`specs_canon.py::_CANON_FILE_PATTERNS`, `^releases/_archive/releases_histo\.jsonl$`) -- but `specs/releases/` is deliberately absent from `_SPECS_ADDITIVE_PREFIXES` (correctly: the LIVE release tree must stay MUTATING), so it falls through to MUTATING.

**Practical difference is small and fails closed:** MUTATING is still allowed, with advisory presence; the only divergence is that a session self-bound in READ mode is blocked from appending to `releases_histo.jsonl` while the other three histo files stay writable. It never grants a write the law refuses.

Adding a `*_histo.jsonl` suffix rule to the classifier would re-introduce exactly the special-case branch 245d1416 just deleted.

findings.message: DECISIVE EVIDENCE -- the operator's history rewrite is verified clean: the push gate exits 0 on this head in BOTH the PR-range and the whole-history shapes, closing the prior cycle's 11 offending objects including three commit messages.
findings.detail_md:
Reproduced exactly as the pre-push hook runs it, from the repository root:

```
# PR-range shape (remote = origin/develop)
printf 'refs/heads/feature/0.5.0 %s refs/heads/feature/0.5.0 %s\n' "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" "$(git rev-parse origin/develop)" \
  | <venv>/bin/dadaia ci push-gate-check
-> [pre-push] denylist scan mode: operator denylist + baseline
-> exit 0

# New-branch shape (remote = 40 zeros -> whole history scanned)
printf 'refs/heads/feature/0.5.0 %s refs/heads/feature/0.5.0 %s\n' "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" "$(printf '0%.0s' {1..40})" \
  | <venv>/bin/dadaia ci push-gate-check
-> exit 0
```

The prior verdict for this release (metrics.carried_from) was explicitly CONDITIONAL on this rewrite and recorded 11 offending objects, three of which were commit MESSAGES that a tree-only rewrite would have left published. All 11 are gone. The venv is an editable install resolving to this working tree, so the scanner that ran is this diff's own code, not a released copy.

Both shapes were re-run and re-confirmed at each of the four heads this review tracked (f7078c93 -> 412ef54a -> 38718901 -> 95bc2e56 -> 4391713f -> fa021900 -> 99e30d4f -> b0fd592e), including this one. The specs-canon predicates were also evaluated directly against the head tree's 52 `specs/` paths: `canon_violations -> []`, `verdict_violations(head, first-parent) -> []`.

**Re-key 4 (this one), 4391713f.** The delta from 95bc2e56 is a single commit, `style: ruff --fix (unused import left by the win32 skip marker)`, touching one file: `tests/contract/test_pr_verdict_check_gate.py`, moving `import sys` above `from pathlib import Path`. Import ORDER only -- no statement added, removed or changed. `git diff --name-only 95bc2e56..HEAD -- dadaia_workspace/ .github/ pyproject.toml poetry.lock` returns **zero files**, so no production, workflow, script or dependency surface moved and every finding below carries over unchanged. Both push-gate shapes re-run at exit 0, `canon_violations`/`verdict_violations` on the 52 `specs/` paths return `[]`/`[]`, and the same 383 targeted tests pass.

**Re-key 5 (final), fa021900.** Delta from 4391713f is three commits: `245d1416` (production -- the FROZEN deletion, reviewed as production and recorded as its own INFO plus a LOW residual), `3df02f55` (specs only -- a RELEASE.json qa-close log record and three bug records moved to resolved), and `fa021900` (test helper -- `import fcntl` moved inside `drain_stderr_nonblocking` so Windows collection of `tests/` stays importable; POSIX-only stdlib module, no security surface, and the exact defect class a top-level `fcntl` import is known for). Both push-gate shapes re-run at exit 0 and the canon predicates return `[]`/`[]`.
findings.fix_recommendation: None. This is the evidence the APPROVED verdict rests on.

findings.message: Priority 1 -- the new pre-push specs-canon gate is injection-clean and fails closed; the git port's two new methods shape-check before interpolating and pass the prefix in pathspec position.
findings.fix_recommendation: None.

findings.message: Priority 6 -- the CI verdict script's canon-derived release-id pattern is anchored, so none of its three uses can be bypassed by a traversal or an _ideas/_archive token, and the bash-3.2 array guards added at 412ef54a were empirically proven safe.
findings.detail_md:
The load-bearing question for `.github/scripts/pr-verdict-check.sh` is whether the pattern it derives at runtime is anchored -- an unanchored ERE would let `RELEASE_ID` carry a traversal prefix and still match. It is:

```
core/specs_version.py::release_semver_ere_pattern()
  -> ^v?[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(-[0-9A-Za-z][0-9A-Za-z.]*)?$
```

Both `^` and `$` present, and bash's `[[ =~ ]]` applies POSIX ERE without REG_NEWLINE, so `$` is end-of-string, not end-of-line. That single anchored pattern guards all three trust decisions: the `RELEASE_ID` narrowing (`:172-178`), `_is_verdict_evidence_path`'s id segment (`:192-203`), and the per-glob-hit release-id segment filter (`:236-254`). The right-hand operand is correctly left unquoted at every use, and `[[ ]]` performs no word splitting or globbing on it. The derivation itself is fail-closed with no fallback glob (`:138-160`), and `PYTHONPATH` is self-located from `BASH_SOURCE[0]` rather than the caller's cwd.

The 412ef54a delta swaps four array expansions to the `${arr[@]+"${arr[@]}"}` form and adds an unset-safe emptiness guard. Proven empirically rather than assumed:

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| element named `a b.handoff.json` | boundary preserved, one iteration |
| element named `x*y.handoff.json` | passed through literally, no re-globbing |
| empty array under `set -u` | zero iterations, no unbound-variable abort |
| emptiness guard on a 0-element array | expands to the empty string -> `exit 1`, fail closed |
| emptiness guard on a 2-element array | expands to `2` -> proceeds |

findings.message: Re-key onto the develop merge is proven by TREE IDENTITY, not by inspection: HEAD and the previously approved sha share one tree object, so the merge introduced zero content.

A merge is the one operation in this flow that can bring unreviewed content into a branch without appearing as authored work, so I did not accept the hand-off's 'content this branch already had' claim -- I proved it.

```
git rev-parse fa021900^{tree}  -> d50530be21c61e4a24e839968efca7a4ad618b4a
git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}      -> d50530be21c61e4a24e839968efca7a4ad618b4a
git diff fa021900..HEAD        -> (empty, ALL paths)
```

Tree identity is stronger than any path-scoped diff: it covers every file in the repository at once, so no path -- inside or outside `dadaia_workspace`/`.github`/`tests` -- can carry a surprise. Every finding in this handoff therefore transfers unchanged; there is no delta to review.

|---|---|---|

**Diff-base consequence.** `origin/develop` is now an ancestor of HEAD (`git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/develop HEAD` succeeds, and the merge base IS b1fc8f29), so the two-dot and three-dot diffs coincide and the PR range is fully reconciled. It exits 0, as does the PR-range shape. `canon_violations` and `verdict_violations` on the 52 `specs/` paths both return `[]`.

findings.message: Closure re-key proven by SUBTREE HASH IDENTITY on the three reviewed surfaces, and the archived evidence location verified against both gates before it was written.
findings.detail_md:
**Nothing reviewed moved.** Rather than re-reading a rename-heavy diff, I compared tree objects directly:

| Subtree | 48d032dc | HEAD | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dadaia_workspace` | `319414093339` | `319414093339` | IDENTICAL |
| `.github` | `aa03a67faf95` | `aa03a67faf95` | IDENTICAL |
| `tests` | `cde2785024eb` | `cde2785024eb` | IDENTICAL |

`git diff 48d032dc..HEAD -- dadaia_workspace .github tests` is empty, and the same three subtrees are ALSO identical between `origin/develop` and HEAD — so the develop -> main closure PR carries no production content beyond the rc-1 body already reviewed. Every finding transfers unchanged.

**The closure delta, in full:** 5 files, +34/-219, zero paths outside `specs/`.

| Path | Change |
|---|---|
| `specs/releases/{ => _archive}/0.5.0/SPEC.md` | pure rename, 0 changed lines |
| `specs/releases/{ => _archive}/0.5.0/PLAN.md` | pure rename, 0 changed lines |
| `specs/releases/{ => _archive}/0.5.0/RELEASE.json` | rename + phase ARCHIVED, rc 1, `implemented {48d032dc, rc 1}`, 2 log records |
| `specs/releases/{ => _archive}/0.5.0/TASKS.md` | rename + markers T-050-02/14/37/38/41 closed |
| `specs/releases/0.5.0/verdicts/99e30d4f....handoff.json` | DELETED (-210) — the consumed rc-1 verdict, exactly as DADAIA.md requires of the consuming merge |

The 34 added lines were scanned with the packaged baseline and the 18 operator terms: **0 hits each**.

**Why the evidence is in `_archive/`, and why that is correct.** I verified the destination against both gates BEFORE writing there:

* `core/specs_version.VERDICT_EVIDENCE_ROOT_TEMPLATES` exports exactly two roots, and the second is `specs/releases/_archive/{glob}/verdicts` — so `pr-verdict-check.sh` globs the archive as a first-class evidence root, which is precisely why a closure PR against an already-archived release is gateable at all (the bug `verdict-gate-cannot-resolve-evidence-after-release-archive` exists because this once was not true).
* `specs_canon.is_canon_path('releases/_archive/0.5.0/verdicts/<40hex>.handoff.json')` returns **True**, admitted by the `^releases/_archive/{SEMVER}/.+$` pattern.
* `_is_verdict_evidence_path` in the CI script carries a dedicated `_archive` arm, tested before the live arm, with the release-id segment validated against the same anchored canon pattern.

**A material refinement to the recorded MEDIUM on the two verdict-coverage rules.** `specs_canon._VERDICT_RE` is anchored at `^releases/{SEMVER}/verdicts/...`, which the `_archive/` segment does not match — verified: `verdict_violations` returns `[]` for an archived verdict path under ANY head/parent pair, and returns a violation for the equivalent live path. So the at-most-one / head-or-first-parent staleness rule **does not reach the archive at all**. Two consequences, both worth knowing: (a) this closure verdict is exempt from that rule, so the 'must be the last commit before the push' constraint does NOT bind here as it did on the rc-1 verdict; (b) conversely, nothing mechanically enforces DADAIA.md's 'never leave a PR-cycle verdict on disk once its PR has merged' once a verdict lives in the archive — that deletion is discipline plus the audit lane, not a gate. Neither is a vulnerability; both are asymmetries a future reader should not have to rediscover.
findings.fix_recommendation: None blocking. When the operator resolves the recorded MEDIUM on the two verdict-coverage rules, fold this in: whichever single predicate the two gates end up sharing should state explicitly whether the archive is in or out of its scope, rather than leaving it as a by-product of where `_VERDICT_RE` happens to be anchored.

decisions_required: MEDIUM 2 -- verdict-coverage rules: adopt one shared predicate for pre-push and CI, or ratify in specs/releases/AGENTS.md that the verdict commit must be the final commit before the push and that re-verdicting deletes the stale file in the same commit.

LOW (new) -- releases_histo.jsonl classifies MUTATING while the other three areas' histo files classify ADDITIVE. Recommended resolution is a one-line wording amendment to DADAIA.md:67, NOT a new classifier branch.
LOW 1 -- redaction seams for FindingRecord and AdrRecord: add .redact() for symmetry, or ratify that agent-authored audits and ADRs rely on the push scan alone.

OPERATIONAL -- this closure verdict is keyed to b0fd592e28f0f92e82a38a156d380574dadf2204 and lives at the ARCHIVED evidence root, which pr-verdict-check.sh globs as a first-class root. Unlike the rc-1 verdict it is NOT subject to the pre-push staleness rule (specs_canon._VERDICT_RE does not reach _archive/), so it need not be the last commit before the push. It is still governed by DADAIA.md's delete-on-consume law once the develop -> main PR merges — but by discipline and the audit lane, not by any gate.
